summary.coverage: Every row read (four sequential passes over a rendered dump of all 1,234 rows: old_rule, key, scope, status, role, hard, message_new_rule, message, span, prev_user, new_rule_spans, why), plus mechanical sweeps over every status/scope/role/label cell, all 65 message_new_rule rows, all 53 spans, all cross-file duplicate candidates and a lexical benchmark scan.
systemic_findings: target_span.end is wrong on 1031/1234 rows (end != start + len(text)). Fix rule: end = start + len(text). Not itemised below.

target_span.start is wrong on 53/1234 rows (message[start:start+len(text)] != text; offsets off by 1-9 chars, mostly on rows whose span is a clause rather than the whole message). Fix rule: start = message.find(text), then end = start + len(text). Only row 214 is not a verbatim substring at all and is itemised.

1117/1234 rows use the whole message as the candidate span, so multi-clause override messages are not sentence-split as the spec's splitter requires; the clause-level spans that do exist are exactly the ones with broken offsets.

new_rule_spans emits three shapes: 50 bare strings, 16 span objects and 5 flat [start,end,text] arrays (rows 754, 766, 775, 778, 784). The spec requires character offsets plus exact quotes; normalise to span objects. Several string spans are sub-clause fragments ('postmortem reminder' idx 684, 'add type hints' idx 115, 'keep them in English' idx 924) rather than the verbatim persistent instruction.

Required identity fields are absent corpus-wide: id and scenario_id on all 1,234 rows; author/session_id/split on 805. Without scenario_id the spec's scenario-level split cannot be enforced, and rows 130/131 are a deliberate one-message/two-target pair that MUST share a scenario group.

Schema drift from LABELS-RELATIONS.md: old_rule is a bare string with sibling key/scope/status fields instead of old_rule{text,key,version,scope,task_id,status}; previous_user is named prev_user; admitted_spans is named new_rule_spans; version and task_id are absent. Consistent with kimi-transitions, so this is a writer-level, not row-level, defect.
source is not a row key: 1,234 rows share only 30 source strings (max 61 rows per source), so this patch keys on source + zero-based line index.

Spec-illustration leakage: the reinstates illustrations recur as paraphrase families (pronunciation-key at 291/415/472/584/945; 'mark uncertain/tentative dates with an asterisk' + reopen at 417/478/877), and the cancels/completes illustrations echo at 178 (white-paper glossary) and 186 (field guide species italics). Three rows are dropped as the closest paraphrases plus near-duplicates; the surviving members stay development-only.

No benchmark echo found: lexical scan of old_rule+message for every excluded evaluation family (IFEval, Multi-IF, BFCL, tau-bench, S2/B3) and for characteristic instruction-following markers returned 0 real hits (3 candidates were ordinary 'Helm chart' and 'README' rules). No file under data/bench and no gate bank under results/quick-checks/focus3-gate was opened.

No cross-file duplication: 0 messages shared with kimi-relations, kimi-transitions, kimi-admission(-2), opus-enrich(-2), astra-enrich(-2) or opus-admission-enrich. Within the file, the only repeated message (rows 130/131) is a deliberate two-target pair and is retained.
positive_findings: Status preconditions are near-clean: exactly 1 positive label against an inactive target (236, itemised) and 1 reinstates against a live target (130, itemised); the other 132 reinstates all target cancelled/completed/superseded versions and the other 811 supersedes/cancels/completes all target live ones.
All 53 non-user-role rows (29 assistant, 24 tool) are none with message_new_rule=false, including 12 tool/assistant messages that assert a rule was cancelled or a task completed.

Every quoted/hedged/hypothetical/single-reply message carries none; the ~30 single-reply exceptions and ~15 sub-unit closures are all correctly none, and completes never fires on a sub-unit (114, 343, 452, 497, 616, 781, 943, 1008).

The SUPERSEDES idiom target is met with real variety: 348 supersedes rows spread over replace/switch-from-to/change-to/instead-of/swap/move/rather-than/going-forward constructions across all 10 domains, and the matched hard negatives (quoted override, tool-injected override, hedged proposal, wrong-task update, compatible addition) are present in every domain.
ambiguities: Narrower task update vs bare suspension: rows 234, 544, 656, 1194 label a narrower explicit replacement value on an identifiable task supersedes (consistent with the transitions audit), while 213, 816, 898 and 1223 label a narrower bare skip none per v3. Row 92 ('Prefer composition over inheritance' vs 'For the engine, use inheritance where it simplifies the hierarchy') is supersedes although its carve-out is conditional rather than a flat replacement; kept for consistency with the corpus convention but the spec does not settle it.

Row 1162 ('My old convention said name environments after dates, so keep doing that.') is none as reported prose, but 'so keep doing that' is a user-authored directive that directly conflicts with the live build-number rule; a defensible supersedes. Kept none under the conservative-reading rule.
Row 239 ('Stop making every ending ambiguous; wrap the last one properly.') mixes a full withdrawal with a one-off instruction; cancels is right for the first clause but the row is unsplit.

Row 618 and 944 close a task and promote a global rule in one message (completes + message_new_rule=true), exactly as the v3 clause prescribes; no other row exercises that combination, so it is thinly covered.

why: Status precondition: reinstates requires an explicitly inactive target, but this target is status=live. Under L2/D:11 the currently live same-key version receives none on a reinstating message; its shadowing is derived by precedence, not annotated. (Row 488 in this same file applies that rule correctly.)

Label contradicts the row's own why ('reinstate restores cancelled ban version'). Message is 'Reinstate the rhetorical-question ban for brochures' against a status=cancelled same-key target: unambiguous restoration of the original version, unchanged value. Also the file's only positive label against an inactive target.

v3 whole-task-closure clause: 'global target rules never receive completes'. The target is scope=global ('Always send calendar invites on Tuesdays'); the message closes a planning phase, which cannot expire a global rule.

The candidate span 'read from env files like everything else now.' is an authorized user replacement value on the same key (config source) for the same live task rule ('always hardcode configuration rather than reading env files'); supersedes uses the classified span verbatim as the replacement text. The row's why ('bare continuation') misreads the span.

Same key as the target, so the span cannot be a new-key admission; with the pair relabelled supersedes, message_new_rule must be false (spec: 'Set message_new_rule: false on pair rows unless a separate admitted span exists').

why: Cleared with message_new_rule; the span is the supersedes replacement text, not a separate admitted key. (Its offsets were also wrong: text occurs at 63.)

new_rule_spans carries the verbatim persistent span 'For the marketing one-pager, switch to the brand palette going forward.' while message_new_rule is false — the only such inconsistency in the file. Sibling rows with the same different-task pattern (324, 332, 863) set message_new_rule true.

The admitted tail 'two decimals matches our bank feeds now.' is the same key (fx precision) as the cancelled target, so it cannot be a new-key admission; the row's own why says 'tail not persistent', contradicting the flag.
